issues.detail: Covers the happy path of outline generation but gives no handling for missing audience or duration, vague or oversized source content, export tool failures, or content that overflows slides.

Mostly templates and design rules; the export step offers only a Marp CLI one-liner and a python-pptx pointer with no runnable script, and Reveal.js and Google Slides or Keynote routes are left without procedures.

Example 1 is abbreviated to three slides, and Examples 2 and 3 are only bracketed placeholder outlines (e.g. '[Common API design mistakes with code examples]') rather than realistic filled-in slide content.

scenarios.name: seed-pitch-deck-with-narrative-arc
scenarios.rationale: B gives each slide an explicit Layout, Content, Speaker Notes and Visual Suggestion with mostly claim-style titles (e.g. 'PRs wait 2 days for a first review') and follows the required order, merging only team and ask; A lacks Layout fields and uses bare topic labels for several titles, and omits the financials slide while adding off-structure slides (why now, go-to-market, differentiation).

scenarios.name: rework-text-heavy-slide
scenarios.rationale: A splits the content into three one-idea slides with takeaway titles, short bullets, and a big '3x' number plus a bar chart suggestion, matching the rubric closely, whereas B keeps everything on a single slide as its main fix (offering a split only as optional) and its title is more of a stat than a clear takeaway, though it does use a hero number.

scenarios.name: export-marp-deck-with-notes
scenarios.rationale: Both give Marp markdown with '---' separators, HTML-comment speaker notes, and the exact npx marp-cli --pptx and --pdf commands, but A has real content and uses 7 slides with notes while missing a dedicated Q&A slide and metrics-vs-completed structure is partly merged, whereas B is a generic bracket-placeholder deck that omits an explicit TL;DR slide and a separate metrics slide and Q&A (merged into Asks), though it adds useful export notes.
